Body-part and animal-covering word fragments predict a negative contribution;
technical and procedural word fragments predict a positive one. Other tokens
are left at zero, so this captures only a small part of the component's behavior.

BODY = (

    "羽", "翅", "羊毛",
)
TECHNICAL = (

)

programs.haiku:
"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:4225: an "adverb before the verb" detector (negative).

What it does: it goes strongly negative on an adverb or negation (also, just, only, not,
always, still, really, actually, probably, usually, never, all, now, ...) or a
contraction ending ('d, 've, 'll, 're, 't, 's) when it comes right after a subject
pronoun or a modal (I, we, you, they, he, she, will, can, should, would, ...), i.e. in the
slot where a main verb is expected next ("we also have", "I just read", "they usually
shoot", "you'd probably", "you should not join"). It is weaker after 'it', 'that', 'to',
'have', 'there' and similar, weaker still for other words, and zero after is/are/was/does/
did/do, after punctuation, and in "can't". Everywhere else it predicts 0.

Why: the component's activation is almost entirely a large negative spike on these words
(about 66% of its variance sits on |activation| > 0.3), and the spikes follow the
"subject + adverb + verb" pattern. The values are the mean activations per context class
measured on training rows.
"""

READS = ()

ADVERBS = {
    "also", "not", "just", "only", "always", "still", "really", "actually", "probably",
    "usually", "often", "never", "definitely", "typically", "certainly", "clearly", "already",
    "even", "likely", "simply", "truly", "sometimes", "generally", "totally", "basically",
    "either", "too", "now", "then", "finally", "ever", "all", "indeed", "surely", "sure",
    "barely", "thus", "undoubtedly", "again", "well", "both", "mostly", "personally",
    "honestly", "seriously", "obviously", "quite", "yet",
}
CLITICS = {"'t", "'d", "'ve", "'re", "'ll", "'s", "'m", "’t", "’d", "’ve", "’re", "’ll", "’s", "’m"}
# words that make the next word a verb slot: subject pronouns and modals, and the
# contraction endings of pronouns (I'll, you'd, we've)
STRONG = {
    "i", "we", "you", "they", "he", "she", "will", "may", "would", "can", "should", "could",
    "might", "must", "shall", "'ll", "'d", "'ve", "'re", "’ll", "’d", "’ve", "’re",
}
# words that often precede a verb slot less reliably
MEDIUM = {
    "it", "that", "this", "there", "to", "have", "has", "had", "'s", "’s", "don", "won",
    "what", "who",
}


def is_adverb(word):
    """A word in the adverb list, or any longer word ending in -ly."""
    return word in ADVERBS or (word.endswith("ly") and len(word) > 4)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip().lower()
    same_doc = len(prefix) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2].strip().lower() if same_doc else ""
    if word in ("'t", "’t") and prev == "can":  # "can't" does not behave like the others
        return carry, 0.0
    if is_adverb(word):
        if prev in STRONG:
            return carry, -1.6
        if prev in MEDIUM:
            return carry, -0.7
        return carry, -0.2
    if word in CLITICS:
        if prev in STRONG:
            return carry, -1.0
        if prev in MEDIUM:
            return carry, -0.6
    return carry, 0.0

words, numbers, and punctuation receive smaller or negative pulses. Later
these approach small class-specific baselines. Chat markup and role labels

NUMBER_WORDS = set('''

hundred thousand million billion first second third fourth fifth sixth
seventh eighth ninth tenth
'''.split())
CHAT_MARKERS = {
    '<|im_start|>', '<|im_end|>', '<|endoftext|>', '<think>', '</think>',
    '<tool_call>', '</tool_call>', '<tool_response>', '</tool_response>',
}
ROLES = {'user', 'assistant', 'system', 'tool'}

def category(s, boundary=True):
    if s in CHAT_MARKERS or s in ROLES:
        return s
    w = s.strip()
    if not w:
        return 'whitespace'
    if w.isdigit():
        return 'digit'
    lower = w.lower()
    if boundary or s[0].isspace():
        if lower in ARTICLES:
            return 'article'
        if lower in COPULAS:
            return 'copula'
        if lower in NUMBER_WORDS:
            return 'number_word'
        if lower in GRAMMAR_WORDS or lower in FOREIGN_GRAMMAR:
            return 'grammar'
        if lower in COMMON_VERBS:
            return 'common_verb'
    if w in CJK_GRAMMAR:
        return 'grammar'
    if w.isascii():
        letters = w.strip('_./-')
        if letters.isalpha():
            return 'letter' if len(letters) == 1 else 'word'
        if any(c.isalpha() for c in w):
            return 'mixed'
        return 'punctuation'
    if w.isalpha() or '\ufffd' in w:
        return 'non_latin'
    return 'punctuation'

CURVES = {

    'common_verb': (-0.051, 0.438, 0.492),
    'copula': (0.026, -0.172, 0.105),
    'digit': (-0.008, 0.172, -0.043),
    'grammar': (-0.013, 0.126, 0.214),
    'letter': (-0.037, 0.584, 0.467),
    'mixed': (-0.038, 0.331, 0.275),
    'non_latin': (-0.076, 0.858, 0.640),
    'number_word': (-0.024, 0.422, 0.506),
    'punctuation': (0.013, -0.069, 0.051),
    'whitespace': (0.022, -0.145, -0.010),
    'word': (-0.087, 0.998, 0.806),
    '<|endoftext|>': (0.035, 0.000, 0.260),

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:

programs.haiku:
"""Layer-0 MLP component 4227 (down_proj): an "early-document content word" detector.

What it does, in plain terms:
- It is switched on by the first few words of a document (or of a chat turn). Right after a
  document starts, every content word (a noun, verb, adjective, or a non-English/CJK piece of
  a word) gets a positive value, about 0.7, which fades with distance from the document start
  (e^(-n/20), where n is the token's position counted from the document's first token).
- Chat-template markers (<|im_start|>, <|im_end|>, user, <think>, </think>, <tool_call>,
  </tool_call>) are strongly positive near the start of a document (about 4 at n = 0, about 1.5
  at n = 10) and fade more quickly (e^(-n/12)).
- Function words (the, of, is, and, ...), punctuation, spaces and <|endoftext|> are about zero.
- Mid-document content it stays near zero; the program does not model that noise.

Predictions are in the component's own units (activation = x.V * |U|).
"""
import math

READS = ()

CHAT_MARKERS = {
    "<|im_start|>", "<|im_end|>", "user", "<think>", "</think>", "<tool_call>", "</tool_call>",
}
FUNCTION_WORDS = set(
    "a an the and or but if so as of to in on at by for with from into onto about over under "
    "is are was were be been being am do does did have has had not no it its this that these "
    "those there here he she they we you i me him her them us my your his their our who what "
    "which when where why how all any some each both can will would should could may might "
    "must shall than then also just more most very only such other up out".split()
)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    n = 0 if carry is None or carry[0] != doc else carry[1] + 1
    word = prefix.token_strings[-1].strip()
    if word in CHAT_MARKERS:
        value = 4.0 * math.exp(-n / 12)
    elif word.startswith("<") or not any(c.isalnum() for c in word):
        value = 0.0  # special tokens such as <|endoftext|>, spaces and punctuation
    elif word.lower() in FUNCTION_WORDS:
        value = 0.0
    else:
        value = 0.7 * math.exp(-n / 20)
    return (doc, n), value

"""Model the reset token at a packed document's start, plus a weak lexical signal."""
READS = ()

STOP = set("""
a an the and or but if as at by for from in into of on to with without
is am are was were be been being do does did have has had can could will
would shall should may might must not no nor so than then that this these
those it its we you he she they i me my our your his her their who what
when where which while because about over under up down out off very more
most also just only all any some such there here too back after before
""".split())

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    t = prefix.position
    doc_start = t == 0 or prefix.document_ids[-1] != prefix.document_ids[-2]
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    previous_start_marker = bool(
        carry and carry[0] and carry[1] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    )
    if doc_start and s == "<|im_start|>":
        return (True, prefix.document_ids[-1]), 5.17
    if previous_start_marker:
        role = s.strip()
        if role == "user":
            return (False, prefix.document_ids[-1]), 3.6
        if role == "assistant":
            return (False, prefix.document_ids[-1]), 0.82
    if doc_start:
        return (False, prefix.document_ids[-1]), 0.8
    word = s.strip().strip(".,!?;:()[]{}\"'“”‘’<>/\\|_+=-*#~`").casefold()
    if word and word not in STOP and any(ch.isalpha() for ch in word):
        return (False, prefix.document_ids[-1]), 0.028
    return (False, prefix.document_ids[-1]), 0.0

"""Estimate the activation from punctuation that signals a minus or equality."""

READS = ()

DASHES = "-−–—‐‑"
OTHER_DASHES = "−–—‐‑"


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    mark = token.strip()
    has_dash = any(ch in DASHES for ch in mark)
    punctuation = bool(mark) and all(
        not ch.isalnum() and not ch.isspace() for ch in mark
    )
    dash_punctuation = has_dash and punctuation
    multi_dash_mark = dash_punctuation and len(mark) > 1
    mixed_dash_mark = multi_dash_mark and any(ch not in DASHES for ch in mark)

    value = -0.006
    value += 0.164 * any(ch in OTHER_DASHES for ch in mark)
    value -= 0.221 * ("=" in mark)
    value += 1.729 * ("->" in mark)
    value += 0.288 * ("=>" in mark)
    value -= 0.595 * (mark == "-")
    value -= 0.202 * dash_punctuation
    value += 0.229 * multi_dash_mark
    value -= 2.114 * mixed_dash_mark
    value += 0.348 * (mark == "-" and token.startswith(" "))
    value += 0.082 * (mark == "=" and token.startswith(" "))
    return carry, float(value)

"""Verbs that follow a subject: modal and auxiliary verbs after "it / this / that / there / what".

and is switched on at the verb slot right after a subject:

  * modal and auxiliary verbs (may, might, should, must, could, would, will, can, have, ...)
    are positive, most strongly after "there" and "what", then "it", "this", "that", "which";
  * the copula "is" / "'s" / "was" is negative, most strongly after "what" and "it"
    ("what is", "it's", "it was"), and mildly negative after "that";
  * "there's" is about zero, while "let's", "let me" and "modal + have" are positive.

Everything else is about zero. Each number in TABLE is the average activation of that cell
(the program's prediction is that average).
"""

VERB_CLASS = {
    "may": "modal", "might": "modal", "should": "modal", "must": "modal",
    "could": "modal", "would": "modal",
    "will": "will", "shall": "will", "'ll": "will",

    "do": "have", "does": "have", "did": "have",

            "pron": 0.1, "other": 0.1},

    "s": {"there": 0.0, "what": -1.5, "it": -1.5, "this": 0.0, "that": -0.7,
          "pron": -0.4, "let": 0.6, "other": 0.0},
    "was": {"there": -0.2, "what": -1.2, "it": -0.8, "this": -0.1, "that": -0.1,
            "pron": 0.1, "other": 0.0},
    "have": {"there": 2.1, "what": 2.1, "it": 0.9, "this": 0.6, "that": 0.6,
             "pron": 0.0, "other": 0.0},
    "me": {"let": 0.8, "other": 0.3},
}

# which group the word before belongs to
SUBJECT_CLASS = {
    "there": "there", "what": "what", "it": "it", "this": "this",

}

def _word(s):
    return s.strip().lower().replace("’", "'")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    cur = _word(prefix.token_strings[-1])

"""Approximate a strong tab response and a weaker o-initial spelling response.

Training examples show about one unit for a single stand-alone tab, about
half for tab runs, and much less for tabs merged with spaces. Alphabetic
tokens beginning with lowercase o, with at least three letters, have a
smaller response adjusted by length and vowels. Short consonant fragments
in the previous token strengthen it; grammatical endings weaken it.
Small offsets cover chat/tool delimiters. Individual-token irregularities
and longer-range context are deliberately omitted.
"""
import re

READS = ()
CHAT_DELIMITERS = {
    '<tool_call>': -0.115,
    '</tool_call>': 0.10,
    '<tool_response>': -0.035,
    '</tool_response>': -0.04,
    '</think>': -0.09,
    '<|im_end|>': 0.035,
}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous = carry[1] if carry is not None and carry[0] == doc else ''
    value = 0.0

    if token in CHAT_DELIMITERS:
        value = CHAT_DELIMITERS[token]
    elif token == '\t':
        value = 1.01
    elif token and not token.strip('\t'):
        value = 0.38 + 0.40 / len(token)
    elif token.endswith('\t') and not token.strip(' \t'):
        value = 0.30
    elif token.startswith('\t') and not token.strip(' \t'):
        spaces = token.count(' ')
        value = 0.14 - 0.04 * min(spaces - 1, 5)
    elif token.startswith('o') and token.isalpha() and len(token) >= 3:
        match = re.search(r'[a-zA-Z]+$', previous)
        stem = match[0].lower() if match else ''
        vowels_before = sum(c in 'aeiou' for c in stem)
        vowels_here = sum(c in 'aeiouy' for c in token)
        value = 0.13
        value -= 0.035 * (len(token) == 3)
        value += 0.07 * (len(token) == 4)
        value -= 0.05 * (len(token) >= 8)
        value -= 0.08 * (vowels_here == 1 or vowels_here >= 4)
        value += 0.03 * bool(stem)
        value += 0.11 * (bool(stem) and vowels_before == 0)
        value += 0.05 * (0 < len(stem) <= 2)
        value -= 0.08 * ('o' in stem)
        value -= 0.01 * min(vowels_before, 3)
        value -= 0.08 * token.endswith(('s', 'ed', 'ing', 'ly'))

    return (doc, token), value

"""Decimal-zero detector (layers.0.mlp.down_proj, component 4286).

The component fires on the digit "0" written straight after a decimal point:
"2.0", "1.0", "0.0", "x=0.0", version strings like "__moto__1.0". The response is
large (about 2.3 to 2.6) and nearly all-or-nothing: the same "0" after a point
gives about 2.3, while other digits after a point (".1", ".2", ".3" ...) stay
near zero. The point can also be written with a leading space (" .0"), as in
space-padded numeric tables, where the "0" gives about 2.7.

In such tables a leading-space point " ." that follows another " ." (the
"  .244  .174   .0" pattern) also fires, about 3.5. Everything else is predicted 0.

No state is carried between positions; the program only looks at the previous
token, and does not cross a document boundary.
"""

READS = ()

POINT_ZERO = 2.4      # "0" right after "." or " ."
TABLE_POINT = 3.5     # " ." right after another " ." (space-padded table)
DECIMAL_POINTS = (".", " .")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    strings = prefix.token_strings
    docs = prefix.document_ids
    t = prefix.position
    value = 0.0
    if t >= 1 and docs[t - 1] == docs[t]:
        before, now = strings[t - 1], strings[t]
        if now == "0" and before in DECIMAL_POINTS:
            value = POINT_ZERO
        elif now == " ." and before == " .":
            value = TABLE_POINT
    return carry, value

"""Mark a compact identifier immediately following a dot, as in decimal
zeros and code member access."""
READS = ()


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    if len(prefix) < 2:
        return None, 0.0
    previous = prefix.token_strings[-2]
    current = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    decimal_zero = current == "0"
    member_name = current.isidentifier() and current == current.strip()
    if previous.endswith(".") and (decimal_zero or member_name):

    return None, 0.0

programs.sol:
"""Approximate a response to word-internal letter fragments.

Bare alphabetic tokens continuing a word receive a positive prediction,
strongest for short lowercase pieces and later pieces of capitalized words.
Common suffix-like endings and internal capitals weaken it. Script provides
coarser distinctions, and chat role labels after a message-start marker have
a separate strong response. Track the preceding token and the current word's
length, capitalization, and piece count, resetting at document boundaries.
Specific roots and names with unusually large responses are not recognized.
"""
import unicodedata

READS = ()
FUNCTION_WORDS = set('''
    a an the of to in on at for from by with and or but if as is are am be
    been was were do does did have has had it he she we you they this that
    these those my your his her our their its not no so than then when where
    why who what how which all some any one two
'''.split())
# Suffix classes: endings, adjustment, match ends of longer fragments too?
ENDINGS = (
    (('ing', 'ings'), -0.25, True),             # progressive
    (('ed',), -0.25, True),                    # past tense
    (('ly',), -0.23, True),                    # adverbs
    (('tion', 'tions', 'ation', 'ations', 'ment', 'ments',
      'ness', 'ity', 'ities'), -0.26, True),   # abstract nouns
    (('s', 'es', 'ers'), -0.34, False),        # plurals
    (('er', 'est'), -0.17, False),             # agent/comparative
    (('al', 'ous', 'ive', 'able', 'ible'), -0.17, False),
    (('en', 'ize', 'ise'), -0.35, False),      # verbs
    (('e', 'le', 'les', 're', 'res'), -0.29, False),
    (('ung', 'ungen', 'heit', 'heiten', 'keit', 'keiten'), -0.38, False),
    (('chen',), -0.29, False),                # German diminutive
)


def ending_adjustment(s):
    for endings, adjustment, match_tail in ENDINGS:
        if s in endings or (match_tail and any(
            s.endswith(e) and len(s) >= len(e) + 2 for e in endings
        )):
            return adjustment - (0.33 if s == 'ing' else 0.0)
    return 0.0


def letter_value(s, previous, word_length, chunks, capitalized):
    script = unicodedata.name(s[0], '').split(' ')[0]
    n = len(s)
    joins = word_length > 0
    if script == 'LATIN':
        if not joins:
            return -0.014
        if s.islower():
            value = (0.07, 0.31, 0.42, 0.40, 0.31, 0.22)[min(n, 6)-1]
            value += ending_adjustment(s)
            value -= 0.23 if word_length <= 1 else 0.0
            value += 0.15 if chunks >= 2 else 0.0
            value += 0.15 if capitalized and word_length > 1 else 0.0
            value -= 0.39 if chunks > 1 and previous.istitle() else 0.0
            value -= 0.15 if s in FUNCTION_WORDS else 0.0
            value += 0.15 if chunks > 1 and previous[:1] in 'aeiouy' else 0.0
            return value
        if s.isupper():
            return (0.07, 0.30, 0.23, 0.08)[min(n, 4)-1]
        return 0.04
    if script == 'CYRILLIC':
        return (0.03, 0.23, 0.27)[min(n, 3)-1] if joins else 0.12
    if script == 'ARABIC':
        return 0.01 if n == 1 else 0.23
    if script == 'CJK':
        return 0.01 if joins else -0.07
    if script == 'HIRAGANA':
        return 0.04 if n < 3 else -0.08
    return {'KATAKANA': 0.23, 'HANGUL': 0.16, 'THAI': 0.22}.get(script, 0.03)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous, length, chunks, capitalized, position = '', 0, 0, False, 0
    if carry is not None and carry[0] == document:
        _, previous, length, chunks, capitalized, position = carry
    s = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    value = -0.004
    if s in {'user', 'assistant', 'system'} and previous == '<|im_start|>':
        value = 0.87 if s == 'user' and position == 1 else 1.42
    elif s.isalpha():
        value = letter_value(s, previous, length, chunks, capitalized)
    if s.isalpha():
        if length == 0:
            capitalized = s[0].isupper()
        length += len(s)
        chunks += 1
    else:
        start = len(s)
        while start and s[start-1].isalpha():
            start -= 1
        length = len(s) - start
        chunks = int(length > 0)
        capitalized = bool(length and s[start].isupper())
    return (document, s, length, chunks, capitalized, position + 1), float(value)
programs.haiku:
"""Layer-0 MLP down-projection component 4287: a "word-fragment" detector.

What it does, in plain terms: it switches on for a piece of a word that the tokenizer has
split into several tokens, when the piece is a bare run of letters with no leading space
(the "ovich" in "Ivan|ovich", "rost" in "Ten|rost", "ens|berg"). It fires most when the
word so far already has a few letters and the piece is a short lowercase fragment; it is
weak for a lone letter and for common endings such as "ing", "ed" or "s". Whole words
(a token with a leading space), digits, punctuation and CJK characters stay near zero.
Two more cases: "user" and "assistant" right after a chat "<|im_start|>" marker fire
strongly.

It is a rule, not a lookup table: it reads only the current token and the tokens before
it, and uses no per-token weights.
"""

READS = ()

CHAT_START = "<|im_start|>"
CHAT_ROLE_WORDS = frozenset({"user", "assistant"})
ROLE_LEVEL = 1.35
FRAGMENT_LEVEL = 0.5   # lowercase fragment, 2-4 letters, after 3+ letters of its word
UPPER_FACTOR = 0.45    # capitalised or upper-case fragments, relative to lowercase
COMMON_ENDINGS = frozenset({"ing", "ed", "en", "es", "er", "ers", "s", "ly", "ion", "ment",
                            "ness", "able", "ful", "est", "ity", "ous", "ive", "al", "ic"})


def _letters(s):
    """Letters from Latin, Cyrillic, Arabic or Thai scripts, not CJK or kana."""
    return s.isalpha() and all(
        ord(c) < 0x250 or 0x400 <= ord(c) < 0x530 or 0x600 <= ord(c) < 0x700
        or 0xE00 <= ord(c) < 0xE80 for c in s)


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tokens = prefix.token_strings
    cur = tokens[-1]
    same_doc = prefix.position > 0 and prefix.document_ids[-1] == prefix.document_ids[-2]
    if same_doc and tokens[-2] == CHAT_START and cur in CHAT_ROLE_WORDS:
        return carry, ROLE_LEVEL
    if not same_doc or cur[:1] == " " or not _letters(cur):
        return carry, 0.0
    if not _letters(tokens[-2].lstrip(" ")):
        return carry, 0.0
    # Letters of the word before this piece, back to the word's first piece.
    word_letters = 0
    k = len(tokens) - 2
    while k >= 0 and prefix.document_ids[k] == prefix.document_ids[-1]:
        piece = tokens[k]
        if not _letters(piece.lstrip(" ")):
            break
        word_letters += len(piece.lstrip(" "))
        if piece[:1] == " ":
            break
        k -= 1
    if len(cur) == 1:
        return carry, 0.1
    if cur in COMMON_ENDINGS:
        return carry, 0.0
    # Weak when the word so far is only one or two letters.
    so_far = 0.2 if word_letters == 1 else (0.6 if word_letters == 2 else 1.0)
    level = FRAGMENT_LEVEL * so_far
    if not cur.islower():
        level *= UPPER_FACTOR
    if len(cur) >= 5:
        level *= 0.7
    return carry, level
